assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, followed by interrogation at the 1e-18 level) redefined what can be measured and underpins redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. For an experimental atomic physicist this is the cleanest case of measurement precision opening new science, with a clear concept and a decisive demonstration.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice idea and first realized it with strontium; Ye's group drove it to record accuracy and stability and built the frequency-comb and ultrastable-laser infrastructure around it. The two-name list is a natural fair pairing, though the wider ecosystem (Hall and Hänsch comb work, earlier recognized in 2005; ion clocks recognized in 2012) is acknowledged but not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent labs worldwide operate lattice clocks, intercomparisons are routine, and the redefinition of the second is in progress. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes in precision spectroscopy and clocks.
I rely on my own recollection of priority details between Katori's proposal and parallel work; I have not verified them independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum interfaces between light and atomic ensembles (entanglement of ensembles, EIT-based storage and retrieval, quantum memories and elementary networks) are the foundation for quantum repeaters and networks. The ideas are original and have matured into demonstrated multi-node systems.
assessment.attribution: Polzik (continuous-variable ensemble interfaces and entanglement), Kimble (cavity QED, networks and DLCZ-type protocols) and Lukin (EIT storage, ensemble and single-atom interfaces) are plausible core contributors, but the field is broad: DLCZ proposal authors, Hau's slow light, Lukin-Fleischhauer EIT proposals and solid-state memories in rare-earth crystals are not all in the credited set, so credit boundaries are contested.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature as a concept with many independent demonstrations; practical quantum-network deployment is still early, which makes the optimal timing arguable.
uncertainties: The candidate is a compound of platforms (vapor cells, cold atoms, cavities, solid-state crystals) that may deserve different treatment.
I have a professional proximity to quantum-memory research, which I note; this should not substitute for assessment of the credited individuals' decisive contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realization created the first controllable platform for quantum computation and simulation, with enormous follow-on impact in quantum information science. Originality and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: The theory/experiment pairing is natural: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal, Blatt's group carried out the key experimental demonstrations including entanglement and algorithmic work. Other experimental groups (Wineland, Monroe, who overlap partially with the 2012 prize) mean the experimental credit is not exclusive to Blatt.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: multiple independent groups and commercial trapped-ion processors exist. If anything, recognition is overdue relative to impact.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for ion manipulation could be argued either way.
Allocation of experimental credit among Blatt, Monroe and others is not fully settled by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light turned quantum noise reduction into practical metrology; its routine use in gravitational-wave detectors is a decisive demonstration that sensitivity can beat standard quantum limits. This is highly relevant to the measurement-limits theme in precision physics.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the 1981 proposal for squeezed-vacuum injection into interferometers; Kimble's group made the early experimental squeezing; Schnabel contributed to the application to GEO600/LIGO-scale detectors. Other contributors (Slusher, Walls, Yuen, McKenzie, Vahlbruch) are significant, so the three-name configuration involves hard cutoffs.
assessment.maturity: Mature: deployed in GEO600, LIGO and Virgo with demonstrated astrophysical benefits. Interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: The prize configuration could be contested because experimental squeezing involved many groups.
The LIGO detections were recognized in 2017; the distinct contribution here is the technique, which is harder to weigh.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms underpins inertial sensing, gravimetry, measurements of G and the fine-structure constant, and tests of equivalence principles. It is conceptually elegant and directly about measuring accurately with quantum particles.
assessment.attribution: Bordé (theory of atom interferometry and Ramsey-Bordé interferometer), Pritchard (early atom optics and interferometers) and Kasevich (laser-light-pulse interferometry with high-precision gravimetry) form a defensible trio. Chu's related work was recognized in 1997 and Ramsey-type methods earlier, which complicates novelty.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the lab and increasingly in field instruments; large-scale and space-based applications are still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 1997 laser cooling prize and 1989 Ramsey/Paul work could count against novelty.
Whether the decisive discovery is the method or its precision-measurement applications is not fully clear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a new class of matter with robust boundary states and has spread across condensed matter physics. The theory-experiment pairing (Kane-Mele proposal, Molenkamp's HgTe observation) is clean.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe wells following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang theory. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Konig and others are not in the credited set, so attribution is a real tension.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive independent confirmation in multiple materials, though practical impact is still emerging. A prize in 2016 already recognized topological phases (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz).
uncertainties: Overlap with 2016 prize and omission of BHZ and Zhang.
Outside my own field; I defer partly to colleagues in condensed matter for fine details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single NV spins in diamond created a room-temperature solid-state qubit platform and a versatile nanoscale sensor, with applications from magnetometry to biological sensing. The link to measuring small fields with single quantum systems is attractive.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the single-NV optical detection and coherent control demonstrations; Lukin contributed theory and key sensing and quantum-register experiments. Gruber, Awschalom, Hanson and Walsworth also had major contributions, so the three-name set is partial.
assessment.maturity: Substantial independent confirmation and growing applications; sensing maturity is advancing, and commercial uses are emerging.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed across many groups.
Lukin appears on several candidates; it is uncertain whether one prize would be built around him.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides strong coupling between superconducting qubits and microwave photons and is the architecture of leading superconducting quantum processors. Originality and impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Blais (theory), Wallraff and Schoelkopf (first experimental demonstrations in 2004) form a coherent triple. Close ties to the macroscopic circuit quantum effects recognized in 2025, and to Devoret, Martinis and Nakamura, complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense of widespread adoption, but the final technological outcome of superconducting quantum computing remains open, so timing may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the discovery as physics or as engineering of a platform.
